Red Rock Resources Plc, the natural resource development company with interests in gold and base metals, principally in Africa and Australia, announces an issue of 95,238,095 ordinary shares of £0.0001 each in the Company ("Shares") in settlement of a loan of £20,000.
Admission to Trading on AIM and Total Voting Rights
Application is being made for 95,238,095 to be admitted to trading on AIM, the admission of which it is expected on or around 3 August 2026.
In accordance with the provision of the Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules of the Financial Conduct Authority, the Company confirms that, following the issue of the Shares, its issued ordinary share capital will comprise 9,675,142,514 ordinary shares.
All of the ordinary shares have equal voting rights and none of the ordinary shares are held in Treasury. The total number of voting rights in the Company will therefore be 9,675,142,514. The above figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations to determine if they are required to notify their interests in, or change to their interest in, the Company.

Signature of Contract
24 July 2026
Red Rock Resources Plc, the natural resource exploration and development company
with interests
in gold, base metals, battery metals, and hydrocarbons, principally in Africa and Australia, announces, further to the announcements of 1 June 2026 and 25 June 2026, the signature of a contract between the Ministry of Rural Development of the DRC and Koto DRC SARL for
the works of construction and installation of the first factory for manufacture of wall panels for the construction of housing in the province of Kinshasa.
This follows the public tender and publication of provisional award of the contract, which covers a further two factories. Following final award, initial payment for Lot 1, with a contract value of $7,158,887, will now be made to Koto DRC SARL.
Red Rock Chairman Andrew Bell comments:
"This follows a lengthy process whereby
the Company formed a 50-50 joint venture (JV) in November 2024 to operate factories and build low cost housing, made a proposal to and signed an agreement with the Ministry of Rural Development in October 2025, and subsequently in 2026 the JV won an open tender which was then reviewed by the different regulatory bodies.
The final signature of the contract is a significant milestone which permits the disbursement of funds into the JV."
Previous
announcements have been made by the Company as matters progressed, notably on
6 November 2024, 23 October 2025, 11 February 2026, 1 April 2026
, and now 1 June 2026 and 25 June 2026. Further announcements will be made as progress continues on this and other matters.
As noted in the Interim Statement dated 1 April 2026, the Company expected sales of assets and progress in the DRC to support the financial position, which has remained stretched while waiting for these developments. These matters have progressed but not at the forecast speed, so that the Company expects to raise further funds by disposals or otherwise, and meanwhile
depends on the continued support of key stakeholders.

company_30s.what_they_do: RRR.L is a junior mining exploration company that owns copper‑focused licences in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Ivory Coast.  Its main activity is drilling, geological mapping and partnering with larger miners to develop the sites.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Copper is a key input for batteries and EVs, so new sources in high‑grade regions are highly prized.  The company’s licences sit in a historically productive corridor, giving it a credible upside if the geology turns out to be good.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in the exploration phase, with no production yet and a cash‑burning model.  It has been hit by a steep sell‑off, trading near the bottom of its 52‑week range and still struggling to raise fresh capital.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy finalising joint‑venture contracts in the DRC and Ivory Coast, signalling a push to secure working capital and technical support from partners.
Governance and capital structure changes – new equity issuances and voting‑rights adjustments – suggest the board is trying to keep the company afloat.
Financial reporting remains mixed: a half‑year results release shows continued losses but also a modest increase in exploration spend, hinting at a potential pivot to higher‑grade targets.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet with a handful of jokes – the community is largely indifferent and not actively trading the stock.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: No clear bullish chatter – the silence itself is a contrarian signal.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears focus on the lack of production, uncertain funding and the risk of further dilution.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has stayed flat; there’s no shift toward optimism or panic.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the market is not tracking this name, creating a high‑surprise window if a catalyst appears.

near_term_catalysts: A formal joint‑venture agreement signed in the DRC that brings in a partner’s capital and technical expertise.
New drilling results that identify a copper‑rich zone within one of the licences.
A capital‑raising event (equity or convertible debt) that injects cash and reduces the burn rate.
A sustained volume spike above the 5‑day average, especially on a support level near the 52‑week low.
A spike in copper prices that could make the project more attractive to investors.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained 2‑3× volume increase, a drilling announcement, or a JV signing.  A price move above the 10‑day SMA with a 5‑% breakout would be a clear trigger.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the late wash‑out phase of a deep crash.  The APEX score indicates a tight compression, so a catalyst could produce a rapid rebound.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The price is 86% below its pre‑crash level – a huge upside potential.  If it recovers to even 50% of that level, the return would be roughly 3.5×.  RED‑colour signals historically deliver >160% gains, and the company’s licences are in a high‑grade copper corridor, giving a solid fundamental base for a bounce.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: There is no production yet, funding remains uncertain, and the company could face further dilution or a failed capital raise.  The worst outcome is the price staying at the bottom of its range, potentially dropping further if cash runs out.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside about 3.5× versus a single‑digit downside.  The risk/reward asymmetry is roughly 3.5:1.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout of the 52‑week low with a volume spike of at least 2× the 5‑day average.  Allocate 10% of your portfolio, set a stop 5% below entry, and trail the stop by 10% once the price moves 10% higher.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a drilling announcement or JV signing.  If volume rises 2× and the price crosses the 10‑day SMA, consider a small position to test the move.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risk identified – the only real risk is that the company fails to raise capital.  If that becomes clear, exit immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: An 86% crash on a quiet, trend‑free market gives a clear contrarian bullish case; if a DRC joint‑venture or positive drilling data surfaces, the upside could be 3–4× with limited downside.
